full.description: This image is a photomicrograph of a gastrointestinal tissue sample, likely colon. It shows neoplastic glandular structures characteristic of adenocarcinoma extending into the deeper layers of the bowel wall. Surrounding fibrous tissue and inflammatory cell infiltration are also visible. The findings are indicative of invasive adenocarcinoma of the gastrointestinal tract.

random.description: This is a hematoxylin and eosin-stained photomicrograph of breast tissue showing invasive carcinoma. The image demonstrates malignant epithelial glands infiltrating through the fibroadipose stroma. Surrounding neural structures are also visible within the fibrous connective tissue stroma. The histopathological findings are consistent with invasive ductal carcinoma of the breast.

Intraductal carcinoma of the prostate. Large glands with markedly irregular glandular contour intermingle with invasive cancer (a). These glands have much larger size and more irregular shape than HGPIN glands and are much more likely to have dense cribriform (b) or solid architecture and comedo necrosis (c). In addition, the constituent cells in intraductal carcinoma are more likely to exhibit marked nuclear pleomorphism (d). Basal cells are always retained in these glands (e)
